sample_unit: reports (180 authentic plus 20 adversarial) rated by readers; 1025 held-out reports for automated comparison

links.outcome: Model acceptance on authentic reports interleaved with adversarial cases
links.effect: Every output was valid schema-conformant JSON; grouped acceptance rate 100% (95% CI 97.9-100), but one reader judged negative-finding lists incomplete in 57.8% of reports.
links.quote: Every output was valid, schema-conformant JSON, and the grouped acceptance rate was 100% (95% CI 97.9-100), though one reader judged negative-finding lists incomplete in 57.8% of reports.

links.outcome: Fine-tuned model compared against rule-based baseline, base model, and larger model on held-out set
links.effect: Fine-tuning raised impression agreement from 17.7% to 67.1% and urgent-flag sensitivity from 18.8% to 62.5% (p<.001); larger non-fine-tuned model reached 27.5% and 50.0%.
links.quote: On the full held-out set (1025 reports), fine-tuning increased agreement with the silver-label impression from 17.7% to 67.1% and urgent-flag sensitivity against the silver reference from 18.8% to 62.5% (both p < .001); the larger non-fine-tuned model reached 27.5% and 50.0%, and a rule-based baseline 99.0% on body region.

links.outcome: Reader scoring of silver-standard labels versus model outputs
links.effect: When readers scored the silver labels themselves, the model was rated higher on negative findings and lower on the impression, showing the silver reference is imperfect.
links.quote: When the readers scored the silver labels themselves, the model was rated higher on negative findings and lower on the impression.

unlisted_practices: QLoRA fine-tuning of a compact medical LLM for locally deployable report structuring
Local deployment on consumer GPU hardware for data privacy

screen.reason: Evaluates a fine-tuned compact LLM (TurkRadLLM) for structuring Turkish spine MRI reports using a multi-reader clinical validation study including adversarial stress tests, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
